structure: batch-outer (16 batches); identity [128,128] loaded once into SBUF; per batch load rhs[b] resident [k=64(par), n=4096(free)] once (16 KB/part), sliced per n-chunk; per m-tile (32 = 4096/128): load lhs tile [m_in=128(par), k=64(free)], identity-transpose ONCE via nc_matmul(is_transpose=True, is_moving_onezero=True) -> PSUM [k=64(par), m_in=128(free)], copy to SBUF; then 8 n-chunks of 512: SINGLE-PASS K=64 main matmul nc_matmul(stationary=lhs_t[64,128], moving=rhs[64,512]) -> [m_in=128(par), n=512(free)] PSUM (NO K-accumulation loop, K=64<=128 fits one Tensor-Engine pass), copy to SBUF, store into direct 3D output out[b, 128*mt:+128, 512*c:+512]. fp32 throughout.
arg_roles: v1=lhs (16,4096,64)=(B,M,K); v2=rhs (16,64,4096)=(B,K,N); out=(16,4096,4096)=(B,M,N), reshapes row-major to the reference (16,4096,4096). Reference transform_to_nki_inputs is reshape-only (natural batched layout, NOT pre-tiled like dense matmul).
verdict: PROMOTED (phase-1 correctness base / DAG root; no phase-1 perf floor)
notes: First correct Phase-1 bmm kernel. fp32 throughout, full 5-seed L2 PASS (correct 1/1) at 3.8477ms/0.663x over the 2.550ms baseline. Single-pass K=64 (K<=128) means exactly ONE main nc_matmul per (b,mt,c) output tile -- no K-accumulation loop, markedly simpler than the matmul sibling's 40-way K-accum. Traffic at the read-once/write-once floor: HBMwr 1074MB == output B*M*N*4 = 1073.7MB (no spill); HBMrd 34MB == lhs+rhs each read once (16.78+16.78=33.55MB); rhs-once-per-batch achieves minimal reads. Tile coverage exact (32 m-tiles x 8 n-chunks x 16 batches = 4096 tiles, no gap/overlap). Direct 3D output (16,4096,4096) traced fine -- the documented 4D fallback (16,32,128,4096) was NOT needed. SURPRISE vs the phase-1 draft: the draft framed this op as WRITE-BOUND (output 1.074GB @ ~781GB/s ~= 1.375ms near-hard ceiling, above a ~0.90ms PE floor), but the MEASURED profile is PE-BOUND: PE=95% while DMA=only 39%. The PE-active proxy (PE%*latency ~= 3.66ms) sits far above BOTH theoretical floors, so the per-512-chunk store granularity leaves PE/DMA overlap unexploited. Phase-2 surface = the PE-bound gap to the ~0.90ms PE floor (re-frame the draft's write-bound thesis against this measurement); levers to explore: store-burst fattening ([128,4096] per m-tile) + compute/DMA overlap, and whether the fp32 single-pass PE cost itself dominates. Phase 1 does NOT act on it (correctness-only, no perf floor).
phase2_note: draft predicted write-bound; measured PE=95%/DMA=39% => PE-bound. Confirm framing with the round-0 analyze task (Codex) before phase 2.

verdict: REJECTED (--fast screen): D1 multi-batch blocking B_BLK=2 REGRESSES +28% (not a no-op)
notes: D1 primary lever, B_BLK=2: block 2 adjacent batches -- load 2 rhs tiles + transpose all 2*32=64 m-tiles into one resident [2,64,4096] pack (Pass 1), then stream 2*256 main matmuls no-transpose-interleaved (Pass 2), so the Pass-1/Pass-2 transition happens 8 times instead of 16. RESULT: p50 2.6099ms (+28.2% vs bmm_v2 2.0363), TRUE PE-active/inf 2.5722ms (+27.7%), per-matmul stall 0.2955us (+27.7% vs 0.2314) -- a clear out-of-noise REGRESSION. PURE RESCHEDULE confirmed bit-exact: matmul_instruction_count 8704==bmm_v2, psum_copies 4224==, HBM 34/1074MB== NO spill, rel-L2 1.827975e-07== (seed42). MECHANISM: collapsing 2 batches into one long-lived resident block (64KB/part) doubles buffer live-ranges and constrains the affine_range(B) software pipeline; the per-batch buffer rotation in bmm_v2 (small buffers allocated inside the loop) was HELPING the compiler, and the batch boundary was a pipeline-reset not an unhidden bubble. This refutes the batch-boundary-bubble hypothesis MORE strongly than a no-op would. REJECTED per AC-6 (out-of-noise PE-active rise) + AC-2.1 (regresses).

verdict: REJECTED (--fast screen): D1 B_BLK=4 regresses DEEPER (+43%), monotone with block depth
notes: D1 primary lever, B_BLK=4 (per AC-2.1, run even after B_BLK=2 regressed to establish the fixed-vs-scaling classification rigorously). RESULT: p50 2.9182ms (+43.3% vs bmm_v2), TRUE PE-active/inf 2.8871ms (+43.4%), per-matmul stall 0.3317us (+43.4% vs 0.2314). PURE RESCHEDULE bit-exact: matmul_instruction_count 8704==, psum_copies 4224==, HBM 34/1074MB== NO spill (128KB/part resident fits ~208KB budget), rel-L2 1.827975e-07== (seed42). MONOTONE: per-matmul stall 0.2314(v2)->0.2955(B2)->0.3317(B4)us, i.e. +28%->+43% as the cross-batch resident stream deepens. CLASSIFICATION (AC-2.1): NOT fixed-per-transition (would DROP monotonically toward the floor), NOT a threshold win (would recover at B4), but an ANTI-LEVER -- deeper batch blocking monotonically HURTS the schedule. The residual 0.237ms is NOT a harvestable batch-boundary bubble; it is spread across the main matmuls and the per-batch buffer rotation is already near-optimal. D1 sweep hard-stopped per AC-2.1 (clear monotone regression). D2 precondition ('D1 measured as a compiler no-op') is FALSE -- D1 is a measured REGRESSION, which is even stronger evidence against deepening the cross-batch stream. REJECTED per AC-6 + AC-2.1.

verdict: SKIPPED (record-only): D2 precondition 'D1 no-op' is FALSE -- D1 REGRESSED, a stronger negative signal
notes: D2 (explicit ping-pong: 2 concurrent (rhs,lhs_t_pack) buffer sets, prefetch batch b+1 while batch b's matmuls stream) is gated by AC-3/Upper-Bound on 'ONLY if D1 lands as a compiler no-op'. D1 did NOT land as a no-op -- it REGRESSED MONOTONICALLY (per-matmul stall 0.2314->0.2955->0.3317us for v2/B2/B4). D2 would add >=64KB/part resident footprint (like B_BLK=2) PLUS hand-rolled cross-batch prefetch ordering, deepening the exact cross-batch resident overlap D1 just proved HARMFUL. Two independent negative signals: (1) the monotone D1 regression isolates cross-batch resident lifetime as the thing that hurts, and D2 deepens it; (2) BL-20260709-dma-batching-regresses-pipeline -- hand-rolled ping-pong via sequential_range REGRESSED ~2x on silu because it DENIES the compiler the cross-iteration pipelining affine_range gives for free. Codex (high effort) adversarially reviewed and AGREED (~0.8 conf) to skip D2: building it 'looks like chasing a contradicted hypothesis, not adversarial due diligence' -- the ONLY winning D2 would need to preserve bmm_v2's exact per-batch affine matmul schedule AND prove the alternate prefetch is off the hot path, which the enlarged-live-set failure mode makes unlikely. Contrast the swiglu case (deferred lever had a POSITIVE sub-baseline PE-floor signal -> build it, and it won); here EVERY signal is negative. D2 SKIPPED. TERMINAL: keep bmm_v2 at 1.253x.
